clue.text: Star entertaining a small number in Fijian capital

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within your home, so the capital's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Suva is the capital city of Fiji
a, as in 'ten pence a go', means per
NO is the usual abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A celebrity is putting on a little show in the capital of Fiji.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' here means 'for each', as in 'a pound a head'; the Fijian capital holds both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is an exploding star that briefly outshines its whole galaxy.

clue.text: Second group of pupils listened to argument

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, so it is the pronunciation that counts

parts.note: a school class grouping is a set, and the second such is set two

explanation.surface: The class in the second stream heard a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Schools split pupils by ability into sets; 'set two', spoken, gives SET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or heated quarrel, i.e. an argument.

clue.text: It could be a point all writers make

definitions.text: It could be a point all writers make

parts.words: It could be a point all writers make
parts.note: the 'point' is not an argument but a full stop or similar dot that writers put on the page

explanation.surface: Every author has some argument to make.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop, or point, is one of the symbols writers use to divide text, a category example.

clue.text: Reactive power initially applied in 1811-20 in Britain

clue.text: Stubborn strikebreaker taken in directly after broadcast

indicators.note: the second piece comes straight after the broadcast abbreviation

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast

indicators.note: the strikebreaker is held inside the word for directly

parts.note: due, as in due north, means directly
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike

explanation.surface: An obstinate scab was let in straight after the programme aired.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, outside broadcast, is a British TV term; 'due north' shows DUE = directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind, a straight synonym of stubborn.

clue.text: Build up a ship's company, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew, so a crew

explanation.surface: Gradually assemble the personnel for a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate or build up gradually, as interest does.

clue.text: Measure sometimes leading to charge for sailors at war?

definitions.meaning: a dimension, how far down something goes, is a kind of measurement

definitions.text: sometimes leading to charge for sailors at war?
definitions.meaning: this word placed in front of 'charge' names the underwater explosive dropped by warships on submarines

explanation.surface: Something occasionally prompts an attack by sailors during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth is a measurement of distance downward, and a depth charge is a naval anti-submarine weapon.

clue.text: Illegal drug carried in drab vessel

indicators.note: the drug is carried inside the word for drab

parts.note: dingy means drab and dull
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Narcotics were smuggled aboard a shabby boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, a vessel in the broad sense of a craft.

clue.text: Propose to shorten novel after alarming predicament

indicators.note: the anagram follows the first piece

parts.note: a dangerous or difficult situation, a sorry state

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone suggests trimming a novel after a terrifying crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges TO SHORTEN into ONESTROTH; the predicament word goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge oneself in marriage, an old idiom for getting engaged, so propose matrimony.

clue.text: Plumed helmet found in governor's residence?

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
an address is where someone resides

explanation.surface: A feathered helmet was discovered in the governor's mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is His Excellency, the formal title of a governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumed helmet is one kind of covering worn on the head, an example of the category.

clue.text: Man is governed by this oddly trying law rejected by many

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word trying
rejected things are sent back, so the word law is read backwards

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A man has to live by a strange, trying law that most people reject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a person; its ancient parliament is the Tynwald. 'oddly' takes TYN from trying; 'rejected' turns LAW into WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynwald is the legislature of the Isle of Man, the body that governs the island.

clue.text: Worker at home in 'California bar

indicators.note: the worker and the home pieces are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: An employee is relaxing at home in a Californian bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern, especially in Spanish-speaking regions and the American Southwest.

clue.text: King delayed in regular journey over the top

indicators.note: something delayed comes later, so the king's letter moves further back in the word

parts.note: a route is a journey taken regularly, such as a bus route
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is held up on his usual trip across the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delayed' moves R from the front of ROUTE to later in the word, giving OUTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional to the point of being bizarre, i.e. excessive or over the top.

clue.text: Like some horses, the domineering ride it over others

definitions.meaning: a horse shod with nails projecting from its shoes to stop it slipping

definitions.text: the domineering ride it over others
definitions.meaning: to ride this way over people is to treat them harshly and ignore their wishes

explanation.surface: Bossy people ride their horses straight over anyone in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse shod with projecting nails is so described, and domineering people ride so over others, an idiom.

clue.text: Dearth of motor transport in southern business centre

indicators.note: the vehicle sits inside the combination of the other two pieces

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
a car is a form of motor transport

explanation.surface: There is a shortage of cars in a southern city's commercial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's business district, standing in for CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity and dearth both mean a shortage or lack of something.

clue.text: Sleepy old man drops article in part of Channel

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the stretch of water

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, off the English Channel

indicators.note: the article is dropped from the word man

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A drowsy elderly man dumps something in the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland; 'drops' removes A from MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy or inclined to sleep, so sleepy.

clue.text: Slimy mud in one of three English rivers, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by the pronunciation of the river's name

parts.note: England has three rivers called the Ouse, in Yorkshire, Sussex and East Anglia

explanation.surface: There is slimy mud in one of England's rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: England has three rivers named Ouse; spoken, the name matches a word for slimy mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooze is soft wet mud, especially on a river or sea bed.

clue.text: Bachelor writer in paper served with a writ

indicators.note: the bachelor and writer go inside the newspaper

parts.note: the Sun is a British newspaper
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An unmarried author mentioned in the newspaper has been served with legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ commanding a person to appear in court.

clue.text: Person fishing by quiet border, making a start

indicators.note: the quiet border pieces come first, ahead of the word for by

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a rim is a border or edge
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: An angler is starting out next to a quiet edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a start' tells us the quiet border comes first, although 'by' is printed before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimper is someone who catches shrimps, so a person fishing.

clue.text: Principal encounter between fighting-cocks

definitions.meaning: chief or most important, as in the chief road
in the old sport of cockfighting, a match between birds was called by this name

explanation.surface: The headline event is a match between fighting cocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief, and in cockfighting a main was a match or series of bouts between birds.

clue.text: Hard-hearted, unlike Boaz, ultimately?

definitions.meaning: in the Bible Boaz eventually married Ruth, so in the end he was not without her

explanation.surface: Someone is cruel, unlike the kindly biblical Boaz in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Boaz marries Ruth at the end of the Book of Ruth, so he was not 'without Ruth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means merciless, pitiless and cruel, a direct synonym of hard-hearted.

clue.text: Rather like a kettle of fish

definitions.meaning: fairly, somewhat, as in fairly good
the idiom 'a ___ kettle of fish' describes an awkward mess

explanation.surface: Somewhat resembling a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means rather or fairly, and 'a pretty kettle of fish' is a set idiom for a mess.

clue.text: Ultimately efficacious underworld disguise, sometimes

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word efficacious is used

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: In the end, a mask from the underworld works well at times.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark glasses are slang shades and can serve as a disguise on occasion.

clue.text: Possession could be finally in his power

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else
the last letter of the word in

explanation.surface: Possession might, at last, be in his power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from 'in'; 'could be' rearranges N plus HISPOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of possessing something, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Carpet material provided by communist leader

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by a run within these two words

explanation.surface: A rug's fabric was supplied by a Marxist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a tough plant fibre from agave or yucca used for cordage, brushes and carpets.

clue.text: Much-travelled bishop's gone off and dined

indicators.note: the bishop has left, so his letter is removed

parts.note: a beaten track is one much travelled
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A well-travelled bishop has left and had a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop's' reads as 'bishop has'; a beaten path is a well-trodden one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten and dined are both past participles of having had a meal, as in 'has dined'.

clue.text: Represented woman journalist taken to court

indicators.note: the journalist is attached to the end of the court abbreviation

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
ED, an editor, is the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: A female reporter was hauled before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a part or scene is to represent it, as an actor does on stage.

clue.text: Take-advantage of former partner — one in conspiracy

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for a scheme

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone uses an ex who is part of a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to take unfair advantage of them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wine taster initially given seal of approval

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word taster is used

parts.note: giving something the okay is approving it

explanation.surface: A wine taster has started by giving her approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: Endlessly thorough, you finally caught marine creature

indicators.note: the trimmed word catches and holds the other letter inside it
the last letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: a searching investigation is a thorough one

indicators.note: the last letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A rigorous search of yours eventually netted a sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts SEARCHING to SEARCHIN; 'finally' takes U from 'you', which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny, globe-shaped marine invertebrate.
